Hybrid defrosting was successfully conducted in the Copeland reach of the freezer. 13 DE-EE0009686: Ultrasonic Technology Solutions LLC - Momen Project Final Scientific/Technical Report 3. Milestone Requirements: We have completed the first screening experimental campaign and identified the piezoelectric transducers (or vibrational generator mechanisms) that break frost most effectively. The initial testing was very successful on multiple occasions; the system successfully removed most frost crystals from the surface of the aluminum sheet within one to two minutes. We found that vibrational defrosting is pretty effective on various vibration mechanisms and frequency ranges, and the effective operating region is much more flexible than we initially thought. We have also completed the impedance and resonance frequency tracking measurement while frost is growing on the surface. In Q4, we investigated how far de-icing can travel across sheet metal and found it to be successful on a sheet as big as 6x6 inches for a single vibration generator. Additionally, we learned that the motor impedance correlates with sheet resonance frequencies and found that many of the vibration-generating mechanisms can exceed 100% efficiency when compared to the latent heat of fusion of ice. With these tasks complete, Q4 has been successfully met. In Q5, we successfully demonstrated de-icing on ≥5 piezos, achieving a projected efficiency improvement of> 25% over the baseline (estimated efficiency of 3340%). Additionally, the team spent time modifying the experimental setup and investigating the feasibility of using a phone motor-type vibrating mechanism to de-ice. In Q6, we investigated mounting methods for both motors and piezoelectric transducers and came to valuable conclusions. We designed a breadboard amplifier to meet the project's needs and soft-started the work of mounting and building frost on a full-scale heat exchanger. In Q7, we designed and fabricated a > 100 cm2 prototype, completed shakedown testing, and conducted a suite of mounting-study experiments. We simulated the full-scale heat exchanger and began work to test different de-icing methods on the unit. We used the laser vibrometer to gain valuable insights about the technology. In Q8, we completed the development of the PCB amplifier through software advances, selected heat exchangers for testing, initiated accelerated life testing, built an analytical model, completed various experiments, and initiated new experiments. We used a laser vibrometer to collect valuable data and made significant improvements to our frost- building apparatus in the freezer. In Q9, we compiled test data to show an efficiency improvement of more than 25% over the baseline on a prototype with an area> 100 cm2. Additionally, we analyzed laser vibrometer and de-icing data to identify trends; demonstrated that continuous vibration can significantly prevent frost growth; fabricated and tested different vibration methods 14 DE-EE0009686: Ultrasonic Technology Solutions LLC - Momen Project Final Scientific/Technical Report on Mini heat exchangers; and completed multiple tests on the full-size HX mounted to the vibration table.
